Core modelMAERMSEOOS R² vs. meanForecast range|Forecast| > 20%Avg. active predictors

MAE and RMSE are monthly return errors. OOS R² compares squared errors with the expanding historical mean on identical dates: positive is better, negative is worse. This uses a past-only mean forecast, not the realized test-sample mean. Active predictors exclude the intercept.

Stage 2 · change one thing

What adds value beyond additive Ridge?

Lags and interactions are tested separately. The Ridge reference retains only the four additive core inputs.

Dynamic Ridge

Add the three asset returns known at the decision close, plus the previous month's growth and inflation surprises. Forward holding-period returns are never used as lags.

Interaction Ridge

Add Growth surprise × ANFCI and Inflation surprise × ANFCI. This tests whether financial conditions change the relationship between surprises and returns.

Keep the stages distinct

No combined lag-and-interaction search or Bayesian VAR is run here. Review the focused comparisons before expanding the model.

How to reproduce and interpret the test

Download comparison (.json)
Chronological tuning

At least 36 completed training targets. Inner validation requires at least 24 completed targets at each validation decision. Scalers, imputation and clipping are refit inside each fold.

Fixed compact grids

Ridge α: 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 on standardized targets and mean squared-error loss. Elastic Net α: 0.01, 0.1, 1; L1 ratio: 0.2 or 0.8. Parameters are selected per asset using past validation errors.

One portfolio pipeline

Start 45/35/20; SPY 20–70%, IEF 15–60%, LQD 10–40%. Monthly covariance, BL τ 0.05 and risk aversion 2.5. Costs: 5 bp per dollar traded from drifted holdings.

Reserved test excluded

Only holding months through December 2022. The January 3, 2023 exit quote closes December's position. It is not a January strategy evaluation.

Why these results stay separate from the signal study

The added-signals study changes the information available to the original wider-input model. This forecasting-method study holds a compact additive information set fixed and changes the estimator, then adds lags or interactions separately. Its feature set and shared clipping differ from the wider-input Ridge, so compare models within this tab rather than mixing numerical results from the two experiments.

Forecast sample, optional BVAR and limitations

The small one-lag Bayesian VAR is optional and not implemented here. It requires a separately specified small variable system and a comparison with Dynamic Ridge using matched information. SVAR, neural networks and broad tree searches are deferred.

Training targets are standardized separately per asset and converted back to decimal total returns before metrics and BL. Targets are never clipped. There is no supplied cash-return series. OOS R² uses the actual historical-mean forecast error as its denominator. These choices were recorded after earlier research was seen; this is exploratory evidence, not a frozen production model or an independent confirmation.
